newsitem.title: ALBANIA: Albania PM seeks probe after guards storm hospital.
newsitem.headline: Albania PM seeks probe after guards storm hospital.

text.p: Albanian Prime Minister Bashkim Fino has demanded an investigation after members of President Sali Berisha's republican guards stormed a military hospital in Tirana, a government statement said on Monday.

The guardsmen, dressed in civilian clothing, stormed the hospital on Sunday, apparently seeking revenge for the death of a fellow guardsman who died of wounds suffered in a shootout last week in the central town of Cerrik, a government source said.
Hospital workers held a demonstration on Monday, with about 50 or 60 staff members protesting in the hospital courtyard while Defence Minister Shaqir Vukaj talked inside to the hospital's director.
The Albanian news agency ATA said about 30 men driving two vans with official licence plates and two armoured personnel carriers opened fire on the hospital on Sunday morning.
They beat and threatened the hospital's deputy director, demanding to know the whereabouts of surgeons and the hospital director, ATA said.
Other Albanian journalists said there were as many as 60 or 70 armed men and their shooting had left bulletholes in the hospital's facade, although no shooting injuries were reported.
Fino called an urgent cabinet meeting late on Sunday after which the Council of Ministers issued a statement saying that it considered the event "as extremely grave and with unforeseen consequences".

"After hearing a report from the Commander of the Guard of the Republic, Prime Minister Bashkim Fino asked leading officials of the state's main institutions to publicly denounce this unprecedented incident," it said.
"The cabinet members expressed indignation and condemned Sunday's incident at the military hospital, considering it an unworthy and dangerous act for the Guard of the Republic," the statement added.
It said the government had demanded prosecution and punishment for the organisers "of this grave, shameful and dangerous event for Albanian democracy".
The guardsman who died at the hospital was wounded in a gunfight on Friday in Cerrik, about 70 kms (44 miles) from the capital Tirana, medical sources said.

The interior ministry originally said five policemen were killed in Cerrik in a gunfight with an armed gang that had occupied a police station, but medical sources said the wounded brought to the hospital from Cerrik were actually guardsmen.
Many parts of Albania are still lawless after the violent unrest of February and March that saw looting and rioting break out across the country.
Large swathes of the country are still outside state control and gangs, armed to the hilt after an estimated million weapons were looted in the troubles, seem able to roam free.
